newsitem.title: EGYPT: Investors bid for more than 10 pct of Eastern Company.
newsitem.headline: Investors bid for more than 10 pct of Eastern Company.

text.p: Big investors have made tentative bids for more than 10 percent of the equity in monopoly Egyptian cigarette manufacturer Eastern Company, sources at the agents for the sale said on Sunday.
The bids are in the price range 87 to 92 pounds ($25.58 to $27.05) a share, compared with about 90 pounds on the Egyptian stock exchange at 1300 GMT on Sunday, they said.

As part of Egypt's privatisation programme the state's Holding Company for Mining and Refractories, which owns 80 percent of Eastern, is offering 10 to 20 percent of the equity to investors willing to buy at least 10,000 shares.
The deadline for tentative bids was last Friday but the agents, EFG-Hermes, will continue taking bids until about Thursday, the end of the Egyptian trading week.

"The brokers have preliminary orders for the first 10 percent and are now taking orders for the second 10 percent. Starting this evening they'll know about (the level of demand for) the second 10 percent," one source said.
The source said 87 pounds a share was the price at which the agents were marketing the shares.
